title: The Human Subject Within Plot: The Hypothesis of a Finite Set of Basic Mythological Structures, Inter-Plot Barriers, and a Plot-Based Model of Free Will
content: This article examines plot as a mode of organizing individual and collective experience. It proceeds from the assumption that human beings do not merely register events but connect them into narrative structures: they identify agents, attribute intentions to them, establish causal relationships, and form expectations concerning possible resolutions. The article aims to develop a conceptual model linking the problem of plot finitude with narrative identity, political myth, and the practical exercise of human freedom.Rather than attempting to compile an exhaustive catalog of folkloric, mythological, and other plots, the article advances the hypothesis of a finite plot grammar whose elements permit a multiplicity of cultural and biographical combinations. As a working classification, it distinguishes four global processes—the birth of a world, the destruction of a world, return, and salvation. Their subdivision into sixteen plot families and three scales of instantiation produces a matrix of 48 positions. This matrix is explicitly presented as an original theoretical construct rather than an empirically validated universal classification.To describe the persistence of plot-based interpretations, the article introduces the concepts of the inter-plot barrier, inter-plot liminality, and narrative hysteresis. These concepts function as heuristic metaphors for examining the cognitive, emotional, identity-related, and social difficulties involved in transitioning to a different system of meaning. A distinction is proposed between intra-plot freedom—the choice of actions within an accepted story—and inter-plot freedom, which involves reconsidering the very framework within which choices are made. The creative transformation of a plot is understood as a change in the rules by which familiar roles, conflicts, and resolutions are integrated into a meaningful whole.
